name: Claude for Startups (Claude Startups program + Startup Stack)
evidence: Fetched claude.com/programs/startups on 2026-10-10. Page lists Startup Stack partner offers (ElevenLabs 12 months free + 33M chars, ClickHouse $5K, Granola 3 months Business up to 10 seats, Hex 6 months Enterprise, Gamma 25% off, Firecrawl 2.5x credits, Augment $100, Attention 20%, Emergent 20%, 'View more'), bi-weekly 45-min Applied AI office hours, events (Founder House SF Oct 6-8 2026), higher API rate limits for credit recipients, VC-partner path to up to $100K extra credits. FAQ verbatim: 'we're currently over capacity on the Claude Team and $1,000 API credit offers' and 'We're reshaping the Claude Startups program to ensure this initiative is of, by and for startup founders'; 'we'll re-review all applications which may result in a change in the status of some applications'; 'If you've already claimed the offer, nothing changes'. Review target 'within one week'. Credits are first-party Console only (not Bedrock/Vertex). News coverage (tech-ish.com 2026-10-07, letsdatascience) dates the expansion to Oct 6 2026 and says API credits expire 6 months after grant and the Team year is for orgs new to Team.
what_it_does: Anthropic's startup program: free year of Claude Team (5 Premium seats), $1,000 Claude API credit, up to $45K of third-party partner discounts, office hours and events for startups founded in the last ~5 years, bootstrapped or funded.
claimed_in_videos: Free year of Claude Team, $1,000 API credit on approval, ~$7,000 Anthropic value, up to $45K partner stack, office hours, marketplace listing help; only requirement is a company founded in the last 5 years, no VC needed; 5-10 minute application.
reality_check: The program, partner stack, office hours and application link are real and unchanged. BUT as of Oct 10 2026 the two cash items (Team year + $1,000 credit) are officially 'over capacity' and being 'reshaped'; pending applications are being re-reviewed and some may change status. The videos were recorded Oct 6-8 before this notice. The $45K figure is the sum of third-party offers, each with its own terms; the Anthropic-funded part is at most ~$7K. Partner offers do not require the Team/credit grant.
why: Zero-cost, 5-minute application that can return a Team plan (which unlocks Claude Motion beta and pooled up-to-$500/mo API credits), $1,000 of Console credit, and partner credits Haji would otherwise pay for (ElevenLabs, Firecrawl, ClickHouse, Granola). Being in the queue before the reshaped program relaunches costs nothing; if rejected now, re-apply when it reopens.
how_to_adopt: 1) Sign in to platform.claude.com with the Console org you will build in. 2) Open https://platform.claude.com/offers/startups-application and submit (company founded <5 yrs, a domain email that matches the product site, short description of the apps). 3) Expect an email within ~1 week; if approved, redeem codes under Console > Settings > Billing and claim Team seats on claude.ai. 4) Whether or not the cash offer is granted, go back to claude.com/programs/startups and redeem Startup Stack partner offers you actually use (ElevenLabs, Firecrawl, ClickHouse, Granola, Gamma). 5) Diary a re-check on 2026-11-10 for the reshaped program terms.
risks: Capacity cap: application may be rejected or deferred. Team year is only for orgs new to Team; if you accept Team, the Max monthly API credit link ends (one plan per Console org). $1,000 credit reportedly expires 6 months after grant. Partner offers are third-party terms; some are 'X% off' not free. Do not create a throwaway org to apply: the credit is bound to the linked org.

name: Monthly Claude API credits for Max and Team plans
evidence: Fetched both official pages 2026-10-10. Max 5x $100/mo, Max 20x $200/mo, Team $20/Standard seat + $100/Premium seat pooled, cap $500/mo. Covers Claude API (Messages + Batches), Managed Agents, Agent SDK, Playground. Does NOT cover interactive Claude Code, extra usage in Claude apps, Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry. 'claude -p' and the Agent SDK are covered only when run with an API key from the linked org. Eligible after 7 days on plan; claim at claude.ai Settings > Billing > API credits > Link organization; one org per plan, cannot self-change the link. Credits arrive each billing cycle shortly after payment, expire at end of cycle, no rollover; usage never charged to the Claude plan; orgs move to at least Start tier (Build tier if >$200). claude.com/pricing confirms. Credit terms (anthropic.com/legal/credit-terms): no transfer/resale; nothing forbids commercial use.
what_it_does: Max/Team subscribers get $100-$500 of Claude Platform credit every month to run their own apps and agents on the API, Agent SDK or Managed Agents.
claimed_in_videos: Anyone above Pro gets their subscription matched in API credits monthly ($100 for 5x, $200 for 20x, up to $500 Team); creator uses the $200 to run Ducktate's AI features for free; works on any model incl. Haiku 5.5.
reality_check: Claim holds exactly. Caveats the video skipped: 7-day waiting period, credits expire monthly with no rollover, interactive Claude Code is excluded, and the link is permanent (pick the org you ship from). Haiku 5.5 is real: $0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok (prompts <=100K), so $200/mo is roughly 400M Haiku 5.5 input tokens or ~4M Sonnet 5.5 output tokens.
why: This is the single largest recurring free-capacity item: $100-$200/month of API spend that already comes with the Max plan Haji uses for Claude Code. It directly funds the AI features inside the apps he ships (classification, summaries, agents via Agent SDK) and headless 'claude -p' batch jobs.
how_to_adopt: 1) On claude.ai (browser, not app) go to Settings > Billing > API credits > 'Link organization' and pick/create the Console org the apps use (same email on both). 2) In Console create one workspace per app and set a workspace spend limit so one app cannot drain the pool. 3) Point app backends and any 'claude -p' / Agent SDK jobs at an API key from that org. 4) Spend it before each renewal date (Batches API is 50% off, prompt caching for repeated context). 5) If you later accept the Startups Team year, know the Max link ends and Team credits need a fresh claim after 7 days.
risks: Use-it-or-lose-it monthly; credits do not raise Claude Code limits; wrong org linked requires a support ticket; all keys in the org share the balance; usage still counts toward the org's monthly spend cap.

name: Claude Code cloud sessions bonus credit (/claim-credit, $100 Pro / $250 Max)
evidence: Official help article fetched 2026-10-10: Pro $100, Max $250; eligible if individual Pro/Max subscription was active on Sept 23 2026 2:00pm PDT; claim via banner in desktop app/IDE, '/claim-credit' in the CLI, or https://claude.ai/code/claim-credit/104; claim deadline Oct 7 11:59 PM PT; credit expires Nov 4 11:59 PM PT; 'some accounts are granted the credit automatically'; while credit remains, cloud-session usage does not count against plan limits; excludes Projects, Routines, remote-control, Chat/Cowork, Team/Enterprise, trials, past-due, API-key auth.
what_it_does: One-time promotional credit that pays for Claude Code cloud sessions (Anthropic-hosted VMs) outside your plan's usage limits until Nov 4 2026.
claimed_in_videos: Claim $100/$250 by Oct 7, expires Nov 4; setup under a minute; sessions keep running with laptop closed and past local rate limits until credit runs out.
reality_check: Accurate, but the claim window closed Oct 7 2026 (three days before this review). No extension found. Some accounts were auto-granted, so the balance may still exist. If present it is worth ~$250 of cloud-session usage that bypasses the Max limit until Nov 4.
why: Only action left is a 60-second check; if the credit was auto-granted it is free Max-limit-exempt compute for 3.5 more weeks, which matters for a solo founder who hits rate limits.
how_to_adopt: 1) In Claude Code run /claim-credit and open the usage menu (or claude.ai/code > usage) to see any 'cloud session credit' balance. 2) If a balance exists, push long autonomous jobs to the cloud before Nov 4: `claude --cloud "<task>"` from the repo, or claude.ai/code, or the Code tab in the mobile app. 3) If no balance, nothing to do; cloud sessions still work on Max, they just count toward the normal limit.
risks: Expired claim window; credit expires Nov 4 regardless of use; cloud sessions need GitHub access (Claude GitHub App or /web-setup) and run on Anthropic VMs with network allowlists.

name: Claude Code cloud sessions (claude --cloud, claude.ai/code, mobile Code tab)
evidence: Official doc fetched 2026-10-10: available on Pro, Max, Team (+Enterprise premium seats); counts toward plan usage limits; 'no separate charge for the cloud VM'; start from claude.ai/code, mobile Code tab, desktop app, `claude --cloud "task"`, or Routines; GitHub via Claude GitHub App or /web-setup (gh token); credentials stay outside the VM; `claude --teleport` pulls sessions back; parallel sessions allowed; auto-fix PRs via /autofix-pr; sessions expire after inactivity.
what_it_does: Runs Claude Code sessions on Anthropic-managed VMs so work continues with the laptop closed, steerable from phone or browser, with PR auto-fix.
claimed_in_videos: Cloud sessions keep going after you close your laptop and even after you hit a local rate limit (while credit lasts).
reality_check: Holds. Without promo credit, cloud sessions share the same Max usage pool (parallel sessions burn it faster). The 'claude --cloud' flag, mobile Code tab and claude.ai/code all exist; a '--remote' alias is deprecated.
why: Fits a time-poor founder: plan locally, push execution to the cloud, approve from phone, auto-fix CI on PRs. Zero extra cost on Max.
how_to_adopt: Run `/web-setup` once in the terminal (or install the Claude GitHub App on the repos), then `claude --cloud "Execute docs/plan.md"` from a pushed branch; monitor in the Claude mobile app; `claude --teleport <id>` to continue locally; `/autofix-pr` on PR branches.
risks: Shares rate limits; sessions idle out; repo must be on GitHub for push-back; review network allowlist for environments; credentials never enter the VM but code does.

name: NVIDIA Build / NIM free API endpoints (build.nvidia.com, integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1)
official_url: https://build.nvidia.com (terms: NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service PDF on assets.ngc.nvidia.com)
evidence: build.nvidia.com, docs.api.nvidia.com and NVIDIA forums were unreachable through this session's proxy, so limits come from secondary sources (Sid Saladi Substack 2026, Medium, NVIDIA developer forum threads quoted in search, standardcompute.com compliance summary verified 2026-09-02): free Developer Program account, OpenAI-compatible base_url https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1 with 'nvapi-' keys, ~40 requests/min on the free tier varying by model and load, historically 1,000-5,000 trial credits (~1 credit per call) with no official increase path; model pages state the service is 'governed by the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service'; forum: production use requires an NVIDIA AI Enterprise license; trial terms reportedly allow NVIDIA to collect User Content and Generated Content to improve products (no zero-data-retention). 'OpenAI models' = gpt-oss open-weight models, not GPT-5/6.
what_it_does: Hosted trial inference for ~100 open and partner models (DeepSeek V4, Kimi K2.6, GLM-5.3, MiniMax, Nemotron, Qwen image, gpt-oss) behind an OpenAI-compatible endpoint with a free developer key.
claimed_in_videos: You no longer need to pay for API keys; 80-99 top models free; 20-second setup; plug the key into Claude Code or Cursor.
reality_check: Free key and endpoint are real. 'Never pay again' breaks: it is a rate-limited trial (about 40 RPM, credit-capped) under trial terms that are not for production and that let NVIDIA train on prompts; 'OpenAI models' are gpt-oss open weights. 'Plug into Claude Code' is only possible through a proxy such as OmniRoute, which has its own ToS risk; Claude Code's native loop stays on Anthropic models.
why: A free OpenAI-compatible key is useful for evals, prototyping a cheap classifier, or trying DeepSeek/Kimi on a sub-task before paying anyone. Not a place to run a product.
how_to_adopt: Create a free account at build.nvidia.com, open a 'Free Endpoint' model (e.g. deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4-pro), click Generate API Key, then in Python: OpenAI(base_url='https://integrate.api.nvidia.com/v1', api_key='nvapi-...'). Use only with non-sensitive data and keep it out of production code paths.
risks: Trial terms, not production; prompts may be used for NVIDIA model improvement (no ZDR); ~40 RPM and credit caps; keys can be revoked; never send customer data or proprietary code.

name: OmniRoute (self-hosted AI gateway)
evidence: GitHub page fetched 2026-10-10: 74.9k stars, 10.8k forks, MIT, latest release v3.8.51 on 2026-09-30; one local endpoint http://localhost:20128/v1; claims 372 providers (150+ with free tiers) and an estimated ~1.6B pooled free tokens/month 'provider-controlled, not grants from OmniRoute'; tiered routing Subscription > API key > Cheap > Free with auto/subscription and auto/thrifty routes; `omniroute run claude --model openai/gpt-5.4` launches Claude Code through the gateway; providers tagged 'tos: avoid' excluded from auto routing; install `npm install -g omniroute` or Docker image diegosouzapw/omniroute. Not mentioned in any of the 29 theme videos; researched because it is the practical answer to 'how do you point Claude Code at NVIDIA/DeepSeek'.
what_it_does: Local OpenAI-compatible gateway that routes Claude Code/Codex/Cursor requests across hundreds of providers, falling back from paid subscriptions to free tiers when quotas run out.
claimed_in_videos: Not claimed in these videos; third-party blogs pitch it as 'unlocking Claude Code for free'.
reality_check: The software is real and active. The 'free tokens' are other providers' free tiers (NVIDIA, Groq, etc.) with their own limits and terms. Routing Claude Code's subscription OAuth through a third-party gateway is a grey area under Anthropic consumer terms and the 'subscription first' feature exists precisely to exploit that quota; the README's own 'tos: avoid' tags show the maintainers know some providers forbid it.
why: Useful only if Haji wants to run non-Anthropic models for cheap sub-tasks from a single endpoint. Not worth risking the Max account that runs the business by proxying its subscription.
how_to_adopt: If trying: `docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:20128:20128 -v omniroute-data:/app/data diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest`, add API-key providers only (NVIDIA, DeepSeek), and call it from app code or `omniroute run claude --model <provider/model>` in a scratch repo, never with the Anthropic subscription.
risks: Account-ban risk if subscription OAuth is routed; prompts leave through whichever provider is picked; heavy native-dependency install; audit trail is local only.

name: DeepSeek V4 Pro (0813) and V4 Flash vs Claude Fable 5 pricing/benchmarks
evidence: Anthropic pricing page fetched 2026-10-10: Fable 5 / 5.1 $10 in / $50 out per MTok (batch $5/$25); Opus 5.5 $4/$20; Opus 5 and 4.8 $5/$25; Sonnet 5.5 and 5 $2/$10; Haiku 5.5 $0.10/$0.50 (<=100K prompt). DeepSeek's official site was unreachable via proxy; secondary sources (cloudzero, puter, trevorfox, benchlm) agree V4-Flash is $0.14/$0.28 and conflict on V4-Pro: list $1.74/$3.48 with a 75% promo to $0.435/$0.87 that some say was made permanent. Terminal-Bench 2.1 87.9 for V4-Pro-0813 is DeepSeek's own harness number (datanorth.ai, gigazine 2026-08-13); 'no third-party evaluator has independently reproduced' it; Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 53 for 0813. Cline's tweet claims ~1/57th the cost of Fable 5.
what_it_does: DeepSeek's open-weight V4 models served via DeepSeek's API (and NVIDIA Build) at a small fraction of frontier prices.
claimed_in_videos: Fable 5 only 0.1 points ahead (88.0 vs 87.9) at ~20x the price ($10/$50 vs $0.435/$0.87); 'Claude is beyond cooked'; Anthropic needs a cheap Sonnet 5.5.
reality_check: Prices for Fable 5 are right. The DeepSeek score is self-reported on DeepSeek's harness, unreproduced, and a 0.1 gap is noise. The video ignores that Anthropic already sells Sonnet 5.5 at $2/$10 and Haiku 5.5 at $0.10/$0.50, so the 'needs a cheap Sonnet 5.5' take is already answered. V4-Pro's $0.435 rate may be promotional. Sending proprietary code to DeepSeek's API has data-residency implications (China-hosted).
why: Haji's coding loop stays on Anthropic (and is subscription-funded anyway). DeepSeek matters only for bulk, low-risk batch work in apps, and Haiku 5.5 on the free monthly credits is cheaper to operate than any DeepSeek plan once credits are counted.
how_to_adopt: Run one A/B on a real app task (e.g. 500 summaries) with Haiku 5.5 vs Sonnet 5.5 via the free Max credits before adding a DeepSeek key. If DeepSeek is still needed, use it via NVIDIA Build free endpoint for the test, with synthetic data.
risks: Benchmark hype; promotional pricing; data goes to a China-based provider; weaker tool-use reliability reports; engagement-bait framing.

name: OpenAI '28 days of updates' (Oct 5 - Nov 2 2026): Codex Auto-review free, API tier simplification, ChatGPT meeting notes
official_url: https://openai.com (announcements by Tibo Sottiaux on X; developers.openai.com/codex)
evidence: Secondary coverage (nerdschalk, thewincentral, toolnavs, pasqualepillitteri) confirms a 28-day campaign Oct 5 - Nov 2 2026 promising a daily Codex/Work improvement or a usage reset; Day 2 (Oct 6) Tibo announced Auto-review 'free for all users signed in through a ChatGPT account' and 'does not draw usage from your plan', enabled under settings > permissions > auto-review. One outlet notes OpenAI's Codex security docs still said automatic reviews add usage at the time. OpenAI's own pages (platform.openai.com, developers.openai.com, help.openai.com) were unreachable via proxy, so the 'Build/Launch/Grow' tier names could not be confirmed from a primary source.

name: OpenAI Decisions API (gpt-6-luna) and TypeSafe Jev decision model
evidence: Multiple reports (letsdatascience, propakistani 2026-10-07, aiweekly, Vercel changelog adding it to AI Gateway) say the Decisions API moved from DevDay limited preview (Sept 29 2026) to public beta on Oct 6 2026: endpoint /v1/decisions, only model gpt-6-luna, text+image input, outputs predicates/choices/scores with confidence, priced $0.10 per 1M input tokens with output/cache free, 'up to 10x faster than Responses API' (OpenAI's own figure). The New Stack's '150 ms' is from its Sept 29 article. Jev (TypeSafe): secondary sources (requesty, lilting.ch, towardsai, gradually.ai) give $0.042 per 1M input, output free, waitlist/early access, no self-host, outputs Choice/Score/Noul with probabilities; testers note wrong answers still >70% confidence and prompt-injection exposure. typesafe.ai and platform.openai.com unreachable via proxy.
what_it_does: Non-generative 'pick one of N options with a confidence' endpoints for routing, triage and classification at very low cost and latency.
claimed_in_videos: OpenAI 'killed' Jev with a same-thing Decisions API built on Luna; returns predefined answers with confidence in 150 ms; pricing unknown; lesson: a feature is one keynote away from death.
reality_check: Mostly holds: Decisions API is now public beta with published pricing ($0.10/1M input). Jev still exists on a waitlist at ~$0.042/1M. Confidence calibration is unverified for both. The same job is doable today with Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.10 in / $0.50 out) plus a tool-use enum, paid for by the free Max API credits.
why: Cheap constrained-choice calls are exactly the routing/triage layer an app needs (lead routing, intent detection, gating agent actions). Worth a 1-hour bake-off, but on Haiku 5.5 first because it is already free to Haji.
how_to_adopt: Build a 200-example labeled set from a real app flow; run Haiku 5.5 with a single tool whose schema is an enum plus a 0-1 confidence; measure accuracy/latency/cost. Only if it falls short, test /v1/decisions with an OpenAI key ($0.10/1M input) and compare. Log low-confidence cases to a human queue.
risks: Vendor lock-in for a thin feature; uncalibrated confidence; prompt injection in classified text; OpenAI beta terms may change; the strategic warning in the video (don't be a feature) applies to Haji's own ideas.

name: OpenAI Marketplace (enterprise commitment spend on partner products)

evidence: labs.google unreachable via proxy; secondary coverage (the-decoder, enter.co, pasqualepillitteri) describes three Gemini-powered Google Labs experiments, free, about 15 languages (not 20+), with Google's own note that slang may be misused or invented.

name: MarkItDown (microsoft/markitdown) and markitdown-mcp
evidence: GitHub fetched 2026-10-10: 189.3k stars, 14.1k forks, MIT, latest release v0.1.8 (21 Sept, year not shown; the video saw 0.1.6 so this is newer); supports PDF, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX, images (EXIF + OCR), optional llm_client for image descriptions, markitdown-ocr plugin. markitdown-mcp README: `pip install markitdown-mcp`, stdio by default or `--http --port 3001`, no authentication, runs with the launching user's privileges and can read any file/network the user can; recommends Docker isolation.
what_it_does: Converts office docs, PDFs and images to Markdown for LLM ingestion, with an MCP server wrapper.
claimed_in_videos: Cuts token usage by up to 70%; 161K stars; MCP integration makes Claude convert files automatically.
reality_check: Repo is real and even bigger than claimed. The 70% figure is unsourced; Claude Code already reads PDFs natively, so savings depend on file type (biggest win on XLSX/PPTX/DOCX, which Claude Code's Read tool does not parse). The MCP server works over stdio with Claude Desktop/Code but has no auth and broad file access.
why: Cheap win for a founder who feeds spreadsheets, decks and Word docs into Claude Code: `pip install markitdown` and a one-line conversion avoids pasting binary files into context.
how_to_adopt: `pipx install 'markitdown[all]'` then `markitdown deck.pptx > deck.md` before reading it in Claude Code; optionally `claude mcp add markitdown -- markitdown-mcp` (stdio) for on-demand conversion; keep it stdio-only, never --http on a shared host.
risks: MCP server has no auth and full user privileges; OCR needs an LLM client; token-saving claims are marketing.

name: Granola (AI meeting notes)

Granola appears in the Claude Startup Stack as '3 months of Business free, up to 10 seats'. The TikTok is a paid partnership (#GranolaPartner, code CATGPT).

name: Town (AI chief of staff / 'Townie')

Third-party reviews (usecarly 2026, chorus.com, get-alfred.ai, futuretools) describe a free plan (30 chats/mo, all integrations, weekly briefing) and credit-based paid tiers Starter $15/mo (1,250 credits), Pro $49, Power $99, Power Plus $199; each user gets a Townie with its own @town.com email; Google Workspace (Outlook support disputed); never sends email/invites without approval by default, autonomy adjustable per tool. claimed_in_videos: Not sponsored; ~$20/month; nails your voice in drafts; escalates calendar decisions with a yes/no notification; gets an A.

name: Instinct (personal AI agent over iMessage/SMS)
official_url: no public site found; early access via waitlist/invite
evidence: TechCrunch, citybiz, dealroom, officechai, under30ceo (Oct 2026): $1B Series C at $10B valuation led by Sequoia, Benchmark, Coatue, about a month after a $250M Series B at $2.5B; founder/CEO Noah Shinn (Reflexion paper author); ~14 employees; remains in early access / invite-only; no mobile app, works over SMS/iMessage; group chats opened Oct 5 2026; Forbes-sourced complaints that it kept accessing Gmail and retained emails with financial data after disconnect.
